FRENCH — MOCK EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. fenêtre
   B. livre
   C. chaise
   D. porte

2. When practising Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing.

3. When practising Listening for Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Vocabulary.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Vocabulary.

4. When practising Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Information.

5. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.

6. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.

7. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.

8. When practising Grammar, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar.

9. When practising Oral expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Oral expression.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Oral expression.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expression.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Oral expression.

10. When practising Persuasive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Persuasive speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Persuasive speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Persuasive speaking.

11. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Excuse me
   B. Good morning / hello
   C. Good night only
   D. Thank you

12. When practising Listening for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Comprehension.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for Information and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Interactive Speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Oral expression and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Persuasive speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
